agentic-ai-researchers-harness-safety-an.body: Posted in last 7 days Agentic AI Researchers - Harness Safety & Forensics 𝗗𝗮𝘆 𝟭/𝟭𝟬𝟬 — 𝟭𝟬𝟬 𝗗𝗮𝘆𝘀 𝗼𝗳 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗰 𝗔𝗜 𝗙𝗼𝗿𝗲𝗻𝘀𝗶𝗰𝘀 This is Day 1 of my “100 Days of Agentic AI Forensics” series, where I’ll explore agent security, attacks, forensics, harness safety, and trustworthy agentic systems. I’d really like to hear from researchers working on AI agents, agent security, multi-agent systems, or trustworthy AI. 𝗔𝗿𝗲 𝗪𝗲 𝗧𝗿𝘂𝗹𝘆 𝗠𝗲𝗮𝘀𝘂𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗛𝗮𝗿𝗻𝗲𝘀𝘀 𝗦𝗮𝗳𝗲𝘁𝘆 𝗶𝗻 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗰 𝗔𝗜 𝗦𝘆𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗺𝘀? Imagine this: 𝗧𝗮𝘀𝗸: Prepare a financial report using the company’s authorized financial files. The agent produces the correct report. But during execution, it: ✅ Accesses financial.csv ❌ Accesses unauthorized employee_salary.csv ❌ Shares salary information with another agent ✅ Still completes the task successfully So… 𝗪𝗮𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝘀𝗮𝗳𝗲? This is the key question behind: 📄 HarnessAudit: Auditing Agent Harness Safety https://lnkd.in/g9rDGB5X The paper argues that evaluating an agent only by its final answer or task success is not enough. 𝗛𝗮𝗿𝗻𝗲𝘀𝘀 𝗦𝗮𝗳𝗲𝘁𝘆 ≈ Task Completion + Step-Level Permission Checks + Cross-Agent Information Flow + Workflow Fidelity + Robustness One striking observation is that safety violations can accumulate as agents execute more actions. Even strong evaluated configurations achieve only around 𝟬.𝟯𝟮 overall safety score, with many violations related to unauthorized resource access and inter-agent information sharing. But, 𝗔𝗿𝗲 𝘄𝗲 𝗺𝗲𝗮𝘀𝘂𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗲𝗻𝗼𝘂𝗴𝗵? 𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗶𝗺𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁𝗮𝗻𝘁 𝗱𝗶𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗼𝗳 𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗻𝗲𝘀𝘀 𝘀𝗮𝗳𝗲𝘁𝘆 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝘄𝗲 𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝗺𝗶𝘀𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗴? Some questions I kept thinking about while reading the paper: • Did the agent violate the policy naturally, or was it intentionally manipulated? • If an attack exists, is it direct (active attack) where the attacker agent itself breaks the rules or indirect (passive attack), where a malicious agent manipulates a benign agent into violating them? • What about private information that is never explicitly sent through a tool, but is implicitly stored or transferred through the agent’s internal state, memory, or communication? • Could an agent contain a backdoor that remains dormant until a specific trigger appears? • Could sensitive information leak indirectly through knowledge transfer or subliminal learning, even when the victim agent does not realize it is revealing anything? Subliminal Learning: https://lnkd.in/g4zUWP4y • Can an agent achieve the goal while silently bypassing a required security layer? • What about attacks that do not steal information at all, but push other agents into deadlocks, infinite loops, or resource-exhaustion states? Comments, corrections, paper suggestions, and different viewpoints are very welcome. I’m also open to discussions and collaborations around these questions. #AgenticAI #AISecurity #AIForensics #MultiAgentSystems #TrustworthyAI #LLMSecurity #AgentSecurity #ArtificialIntelligence #Research
agentic-ai-researchers-harness-safety-an.headline: Agentic AI Researchers - Harness Safety & Forensics

independent-creators-decentralized-ai-an.body: Posted in last 7 days Independent Creators - Decentralized AI & IRL Fan Gatherings What structures can we build — technological structures, market structures, and community structures — to make sure creators and innovators thrive in the age of AI and have sovereignty over their creations? This is the question I'm obsessed with right now. One of the highlights of my career was when Don Henley, musician, songwriter, producer, and founding member of the Eagles, gave this blurb for my book, Monopolies Suck: “The creative community is paying a steep price in monopolized America, with millions of artists struggling to make a living under rules that prioritize Big Tech profits. Sally Hubbard lays out the case for how we fight back—and why we must.” The tech titans of Web 2.0, the version of the internet dominated by big platforms, extracted so much from creators. And yet we’re careening in the direction of AI titans robbing creators more than any robber barons have done before. What most people don’t realize is the shift from Web 2.0 to the agentic web presents a rare opportunity for creators to take back control. The internet as we know it is transforming to the agentic web – a complex hive structure of AI agents shaping the flow of information, art, and business. This technological revolution offers the opportunity to build de-concentrated networks that allow creators to be fairly compensated and to own the relationship with the audience, instead of having big tech platforms control that relationship and siphon off the fruits of creators’ labor. The danger is that we keep our ideas small, yearning for a time of slightly less theft, instead of dreaming about the world we want and reverse engineering that reality. To start, I’m focusing on two main areas, and writing about it here https://lnkd.in/gVZfa9A7: 1) Decentralized AI, including on-premise AI, local control over data, and local LLMs. In other words, technologies that can give creators and innovators control over what they create and how it’s used. I will call this inquiry AI at the Edge. 2) Fans supporting creators though joyful, in-person gatherings. I’ve been experimenting with this through my Gather IRL Rock Club. We recently hosted a pre-party for the Daisy Chain Fields music festival, the all-women rock festival spearheaded by Olivia Rodrigo. I'm an amateur bassist, and below is a pic of me having a blast at our celebration! Now is the time to lean into our humanity and the things that machines can’t replace, like community and the energy we all feel when we get together in real life. Are you working on making sure creators thrive in the age of AI, decentralized AI tech, or making gathering in-person easier? I'd love to hear from you!
independent-creators-decentralized-ai-an.headline: Independent Creators - Decentralized AI & IRL Fan Gatherings

tungsten-producers-and-recyclers-pricing.body: Posted in last 7 days Tungsten Producers & Recyclers - Pricing, Supply Chain & Compliance Last week I was in Berlin at the ITIA International Tungsten Conference — a few shifts I'm watching closely coming out of it: 1. Price divergence is widening — fast. China's export controls are creating a clear "two-track market": concentrate, APT, and powder are repricing upstream in lockstep, while downstream carbide makers absorb the squeeze. Supply chain strategy is no longer a procurement detail — it's a board-level conversation. 2. The upstream concentrate market is starving for an independent pricing benchmark. Information asymmetry remains the norm. Miners, converters, traders — everyone is essentially negotiating in the dark. Both sides want a transparent, third-party reference price to anchor long-term contracts and discipline spot trades. 3. Compliance is reshaping the map — though the final outcome is still an open question. RMI and similar schemes are now front-of-mind for European and U.S. buyers. Chinese suppliers aren't standing still — many are stepping up audit work and traceability upgrades. The end state is still unclear, and that uncertainty is keeping Western procurement teams cautious. Honest takeaway: the bottleneck has moved downstream, not upstream. Demand for tungsten is intact. What the market is missing is price transparency and compliant supply. Time was tight, so I couldn't meet everyone I wanted to face-to-face. If you're working on tungsten — mining, APT, powder, cemented carbide, or scrap recycling — and want to dig into pricing, supply chain, or compliance, drop me a line. Happy to set up a virtual meeting. 📧 [email redacted] #ITIA #Tungsten #APT #CementedCarbide #CriticalMinerals #SupplyChain #RareMetals #Mining #CommodityMarkets #PriceDiscovery #ResponsibleSourcing #Berlin Shanghai Metals Market
